local:data-only-json-produces-zero-nodes.title:
`kb-build` emits 18 warnings covering ~330 files: "produced zero nodes
and are absent from the graph". DISPOSITION (Ray, 2026-07-29): known upstream
limitation, not a defect to fix here — but tracked so it is not rediscovered from
build output every time.

Every affected file is data-only `.json` inside a THIRD-PARTY cloned source
(`sources/agents/`, `sources/ecc/`, `sources/fable-orchestrator/` —
`marketplace.json`, `plugin.json`, settings schemas). None is ours, and a data
file has no AST to extract, so zero nodes is arguably correct. The content we
actually want IS in the graph by the other path: the committed prose extraction
`sources/extractions/marketplace-inventory-docs.json`. graphify points at its own
#1666 and asks for reports if it persists.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-02 on 0.9.31, by the recorded method (count the warnings on
the next build): **24**, up from 18. Control arm on the same log: 29
`merge-graphs` lines, so the grep finds real matches. The rise is explained by
the build itself and not by a regression — this build added two sources
(`codegraph`, `GitNexus`), and GitNexus is a TypeScript repo carrying its own
data-only `.json` (tsconfig/package/lockfile shapes). The count is a function of
how many data-only `.json` files are cloned, so it is NOT a fixed baseline to
alarm on; compare it only against a build with the same source set.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-03 on 0.9.31: **37**, up from 24, largest single warning
covering 288 files. Recorded WITHOUT alarm, because the recorded method says to
compare only against a build with the same source set and this one is not: 13
toolchain manifests were added between the two builds (`codex`, `mise`, `uv`,
`pkl`, `rumdl`, `taplo`, ...), several carrying their own data-only `.json`. The
rise is therefore unattributable, which is the honest reading rather than either
"regression" or "fine".

Now also tracked as knowledge-base **#131**, because the same build surfaced
something this item's disposition does NOT cover: `sources/ruff` produced **0**
nodes and `ty` only **36**, against `mise` 19,653 / `uv` 20,524 / `codex` 90,797.
Those are not plausible totals for repos that size, so at least one is a real
extraction failure rather than a data-file no-op — and this item's "arguably
correct" disposition would quietly absorb it.

UNKNOWN, and left explicitly unknown: whether 0.9.30 made this newly VISIBLE
rather than newly happening. The message says "empties are no longer cached",
which suggests they now retry and re-warn where they previously warned once and
went quiet — but no committed prior build log exists to compare against, so do
not repeat this as "new in 0.9.30". Re-probe by counting the warnings on the next
bump.

local:label-communities-schema-gap.title:
`label_communities` (llm.py) has no JSON-schema constant, unlike
`_EXTRACTION_JSON_SCHEMA`. Extraction is fixed; LABELLING is still broken —
probed on 0.9.25, 42/42 batches failed. Community names come from the free
deterministic `label_communities_by_hub` instead. Re-probe on each bump.

STILL PRESENT on 0.9.30 (re-probed 2026-07-29). Counts unchanged —
`_EXTRACTION_JSON_SCHEMA` x2, label-side schema constant x0,
`def label_communities` x1 — with a bogus symbol at 0 in the same file, so the
zero is an absence rather than a broken probe.

The cheap byte-identical arm did NOT settle it this time: `llm.py` grew
3070 -> 3115 lines between 0.9.26 and 0.9.30. Reading the diff did: every
changed line is on the BEDROCK path (`_bedrock_response_text` for #2287, and
the botocore timeout/retry config for #2284). **Zero** label-touching diff
lines, so the gap provably cannot have moved — and Bedrock is a backend this
repo forbids anyway (`AWS_REGION` is stripped by `graphify_env.clean_env()`).

Method for the next bump, in order: diff `llm.py`; if it changed, grep the diff
for `label` before assuming anything; only run the 42-batch probe if a
label-touching line actually moved.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-03 for 0.9.32, by exactly that method, from the pinned clone:
`git diff v0.9.31..v0.9.32 -- graphify/llm.py` reports **0 changed lines** and 0
label-touching lines. Control arm on the SAME diff — `graphify/build.py` +168/-27
and `extractors/engine.py` +168/-10 — so the command discriminates rather than
returning empty for every input. The 42-batch probe was therefore NOT run: with
zero changed lines the gap cannot have moved. STILL PRESENT on 0.9.32.

local:mcp-major-pin-is-what-makes-kb-ser.title:
0.9.30 (#2277/#2279/#2291) pins `mcp>=1,<2` in the `mcp` and `all`
extras. That pin is load-bearing for THIS repo, because `mise run kb-serve` is
the MCP server and we install `extras = ["all"]`.

MEASURED 2026-07-29, both arms, in a throwaway venv:
  fresh resolve of `graphifyy[all]==0.9.26`  -> mcp 2.0.0  -> server rc=1
  fresh resolve of `graphifyy[all]==0.9.30`  -> mcp 1.29.0 -> server rc=0
This host's pre-existing 0.9.26 env holds mcp 1.28.1 and works, so the defect
was never a live outage here — it was an INVARIANT-3 (reproducibility) failure:
a fresh clone could not stand up the server the old pin claimed to provide.

TWO PROBES THAT LOOK CONCLUSIVE AND ARE NOT: under the broken combination,
`import graphify.serve` exits 0 and `--help` exits 0, because the mcp imports
are lazy (inside `_build_server`). Only actually STARTING the server fails. And
the failure is misreported: graphify swallows the real
`cannot import name 'AnyUrl' from 'mcp.types'` and re-raises
`ImportError: mcp not installed. Run: pip install "graphifyy[mcp]"` — so the
message says NOT INSTALLED while mcp is installed at the wrong major.

Upstream tracks the port to the mcp 2.x API in #2308 (below). When that lands
the `<2` ceiling lifts; until then, do not "helpfully" relax it.

**RESOLVED in 0.9.31 — #2308 landed, and this repo bumped to it.** The cap is
now `mcp>=1,<3`: `_build_server` binds the same handlers through either the 1.x
decorator API or the 2.x `on_*` constructor callbacks at runtime, and adapts
`Tool.inputSchema`, `Resource.uri` and the dropped `AnyUrl` re-export. Upstream
reports full stdio handshakes verified under both mcp 1.29 and 2.0.

The item is KEPT rather than deleted because its warning has outlived its
version condition and inverted: the ceiling was load-bearing on 0.9.30 and is
not on 0.9.31, so a reader who finds `mcp<2` reasoning in an older branch or a
consumer repo needs to know which side of 0.9.31 it belongs to. The two probes
that look conclusive and are not — `import graphify.serve` and `--help` both
exiting 0 while the server is broken, because the mcp imports are lazy inside
`_build_server` — still hold on ANY version, and are the reason `mise run
kb-serve` is the only probe that answers this question.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-03 for 0.9.32: `v0.9.32:pyproject.toml` carries `mcp>=1,<3` in
BOTH the `mcp` and `all` extras — unchanged from 0.9.31. The ceiling stays
lifted, so this remains RESOLVED. Read from the pinned clone's tag rather than
from an installed tree, which is what makes it a claim about 0.9.32 and not about
whatever happens to be on this host.
